# Vivarium Repository - Comprehensive Summary

### Project Overview

Vivarium is a modern WebGPU-powered TypeScript library for creating and simulating cellular automata in the browser. It provides an intuitive, accessible API that translates complex cellular automaton concepts into natural language-like expressions.

Name: @wonderyard/vivarium
Key Focus: Fast prototyping and creative coding with cellular automata
GPU-Powered: Uses WebGPU compute shaders for high-performance simulations
Browser Support: Chrome 113+, Safari 26+ (requires WebGPU support)

### Project Structure

This repository is a workspace of: the root project, `docs`, and `examples`.

Key folders and files:
- lib/ # Source code directory
- examples/ # Example projects (Vite vanilla app with DaisyUI)
- docs/ # Documentation powered by Astro and Starlight
- package.json # Project metadata & scripts
- tsconfig.json # TypeScript configuration
- vite.config.ts # Vite and Vitest configuration
- README.md # Project quickstart for the end-user

## Development environment

- Use pnpm as the package manager of this repository. Do not use npm or other package managers and make sure not to create a `package-lock.json` file.
- Make sure dependencies are installed before analyzing files and proceding with the task.
- Make sure to run `pnpm execute playwright install chromium` before running tests.

## Build, Lint & Test Commands

Command Purpose
`pnpm dev` Start development server
`pnpm dev:https` Dev server with SSL enabled
`pnpm build` Linting + Vite production build
`pnpm lint` Check code with oxlint (type-aware)
`pnpm lint:fix` Check code with oxlint (type-aware) and fix potential issues
`pnpm format` Format code with oxfmt
`pnpm test` Run tests with Vitest

## Required Before Each Commit

- Run `pnpm lint:fix` before committing any changes to lint code and fix potential issues
- Run `pnpm format` before committing any changes to ensure proper code formatting
- Run `pnpm test` before committing any changes and make sure all tests run and pass

## Key Guidelines

1. Follow TypeScript and TypeGPU best practices and idiomatic patterns. Create modules and functions as needed in the folders they logically belong.
2. Maintain existing code structure and organization.
3. Update TSDocs of main functions when their signature or responsibility change.
4. Update documentation files in the `docs` folder when new user-facing features are added or changed. Documentation reference (api) is autogenerated with `typedoc-plugin-markdown`.
5. Update examples only when new core feature are added to the semantics of the automaton builders.
6. Add, change, or remove tests when functionality changes. Write tests accordingly using existing `*.test.*` files.
